notes: Healthy has parts: a body that moves and rests, a mind that thinks and feels, and friends and family we get along with. Children sort pictured actions (washing, sharing, sleeping, naming a feeling) under body, mind or friends. Words only; no body-size talk. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1.

words: head; arm; leg; heart; lungs; stomach; brain; skin; private
notes: Correct names for outside body parts and the main inside ones (heart, lungs, stomach, brain), and the correct names for private parts said once, plainly, in the same calm voice as 'elbow', with the idea of private: the parts a swimsuit covers; they belong to you, and a trusted adult helps keep you safe. Private means just for you; if someone makes you feel unsafe about your body, tell a trusted adult until one helps. Words only: no pictures, diagrams, body outlines or pointing, and nothing about what the parts do. The private part words are penis, vulva, breasts and bottom; the family note lists them first, offers preview and a quiet opt-out of this one part, and a person reads the row and the note before publishing (Cory, 2026-11-21). Kept short: no more about private parts here. Teacher note: answer a child's question in one calm, plain sentence and move on. If a child says anything about being touched or hurt, listen, do not promise secrecy, do not question for details, and follow the school's duty to report. This row links to body safety in teacher notes only, never in family-facing text. This is the non-sensitive place correct names are first taught, so leaving out any sexual health unit never removes them. A short family note (English and Spanish) goes home before this day: it lists the body part words taught, including the correct names for private parts, says they are said once and plainly with no pictures, and says families may preview the day. Health states these plain facts itself; science reaches body organs in grade 4. Decided by Cory, 2026-11-20, with any reference to sensitive areas kept very minimal; read for sensitivity 2026-11-20 (docs/reviews/sensitivity-health-body-names-2026-11-20.md). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1.

Hand washing in steps (wet, soap, scrub while singing a short song twice, about 20 seconds, rinse, dry; CDC) and the moments it matters (before eating, after the toilet, after coughing). Children do it for real at the sink and name why: washing keeps me and the people I touch from getting sick. Teacher note: a child without easy home soap or water is never singled out; school does the doing. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO5.

A body and mind need sleep to grow and feel good. Children describe a calm bedtime routine (quiet, dim, same time) and how tired feels. Never a demand about how long a child sleeps at home; the routine is a picture list. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2.

Introduces the first look at an influence: things around us can make us more or less healthy (sleep, washing, play, too much sun). Children sort pictured things into helps and hurts and say one why. Foods are sorted as foods that help us grow and foods to have less often, never good or bad. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO5.

Many kinds of food help a body grow and have energy. Children name fruits and vegetables by color and try new ones without pressure to like them. A pictured plate shows a few food groups. No weighing, no calories, no good or bad foods. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO1, HECAT.FN.HBO2, HECAT.FN.HBO3.

Water is the drink bodies need most; sweet drinks are for sometimes. Children notice thirst and fill a bottle. Teacher note: foods and drinks vary by home and budget; never ask what a child drinks at home. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO6, HECAT.FN.HBO7.

Playing hard makes the heart beat faster and muscles strong. Children try short bursts of play and name how the body feels, and take a water break. Health teaches why and the habit; PE teaches the moving, and both units name each other. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1, HECAT.PA.HBO4.

A trusted adult is someone who helps keep you safe and listens. Children sort pictured adults by those two signs, name the kinds of helpers at home, school and nearby (families vary; a school adult always counts) and choose some of their own on a hand drawing. One scripted ask, Can you help me?"
column12: is rehearsed in pairs. This is the first help step: know who your helpers are; it prepares asking others for help (~NHES.S8.2.1
column13: owned in g1-meh-tell-a-helper). Taught in this non-sensitive unit so a sensitive unit can be left out. Serves HECAT.S.HBO7."

notes: Gear and rules lower the chance of getting hurt: seat belts and car seats, helmets for bikes and scooters. Children practice buckling and fitting a helmet on a doll or with a partner. Reasoning grows from rule to reason. Grade 1 skips this topic as its own row and returns in grade 2. Serves HECAT.S.HBO1, HECAT.S.HBO3.

Medicine is only for the person it was given to, from a trusted grown-up. Children sort things that are safe to touch from things (pills, cleaners) to leave alone and tell an adult. No lesson on drugs. Serves HECAT.AOD.HBO1.

words: feeling; happy; sad; mad; scared; I feel
notes: Naming a feeling and what is needed with a frame: "I feel ___ when ___. I need ___." Children match faces to words and say the frame to a partner. All feelings are okay; what we do with them matters. Introduces the I-statement. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO1.

Calm-down tools children can choose, on the one calm-down card shared with SEL (stop, breathe with a slow breath; counting from grade 1). Practiced when calm so it is ready when upset. Teacher note: never use a calm-down tool as punishment. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO4, HECAT.MEH.HBO5, HECAT.MEH.HBO2.

Listening in four pictured steps: look, quiet voice and body, wait, say back one thing. Children practice with a partner who is different from them, in two places (the class circle and the lunch table or playground). Accepting that people are different starts with listening to them. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO7.

Kind words and gentle hands. Children sort kind and unkind acts in short scenes (a child left out, a push, a kind invite) and practice a kind thing to say and do. The first step on bullying: unkind acts hurt and an adult can help. Characters vary in family, ability and culture. Serves HECAT.V.HBO1, HECAT.V.HBO3, HECAT.MEH.HBO7.

The first decision step: notice there is a choice (the ball rolls toward the road, a stove is hot, a gate is open). Children stop and name "I have a choice." Choosing is taught from grade 1. Serves HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5.

The first goal step: pick one healthy habit to try from a short safe list (washing, water, sleep routine, time outside, asking for help). Children draw it. Never a goal about weight, body shape or food limits; a character's goal is always an option. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2.

Smoke and vapor are not good for lungs, so children stay away from them and tell a grown-up if they find a vape or cigarette. No scare images; the fact is simple and the action is "stay away and tell". Grade 1 skips tobacco and the topic returns in grade 2. Serves HECAT.T.HBO1, HECAT.T.HBO2.

words: private; safe touch; unsafe touch; tell
notes: Sensitive unit (removable). Teacher note: a family note goes home first; school or family may leave this out, the course still reaches trusted helpers in k-s-trusted-helpers. Body safety in simple words: my body is mine, some touches are safe and some are not, secrets about touch are never kept, and I tell a trusted adult until one helps. Correct body names are already taught. Follow the school's duty to report if a child tells you something; do not promise secrecy. Serves HECAT.V.HBO8.

Strengths that help me stay healthy: I am good at washing, trying foods, asking for help, being kind. Children tell one strength for body, mind and friends on a card. Limits: strengths are habits and skills, never body traits. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1.

How germs spread and how to make getting sick less likely: wash hands, cough into the elbow, stay home when sick, do not share cups. Health states the one fact itself: germs are tiny living things that spread from person to person. No blame for who gets sick. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5.

Ways to protect eyes, ears and skin: sunglasses and hats, shade, sunscreen put on by an adult, turning sound down. Children match each body part to its protection. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO3, HECAT.PHW.HBO4.

words: home; school; neighborhood; clean air; safe
notes: Where we live and learn affects health: clean water, safe play places, crowded or quiet rooms. Children draw a healthy place and name one thing that helps, and say how a clean, safe shared place helps everyone who uses it (personal and community health). Teacher note: homes differ; children describe school and a place of their choice, never their own home. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5.

words: habit; every day; routine; help others
notes: Doing healthy habits every day for myself and for others (washing before sharing snacks, covering a cough, tidying a shared space). Children keep a simple picture chart for a week by their own choice; it is never scored. The teacher records each child doing a taught routine at school (washing before snack, covering a cough). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO5.

words: influence; affect; helps me; hurts me
notes: Moves from naming things that help or hurt to how they touch my own health and feelings (a late night makes me tired, play makes me happy). Influence check: name it, say how it touches me. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1.

words: plate; food group; water; sometimes food
notes: A pictured plate with a range of foods and a water cup. Foods are foods that help us grow and foods for sometimes, never good or bad. An ad on a snack can make it look more fun; children say what the ad wants. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO1, HECAT.FN.HBO2, HECAT.FN.HBO3, HECAT.FN.HBO6, HECAT.FN.HBO7.

Active play stays safe with space, rules, water and stopping when hurt. Children name two safe-play rules for a game. Shared with PE. Carries the kindergarten gear rule: a helmet for bikes and scooters. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1, HECAT.PA.HBO4, HECAT.PA.HBO6.
When and how to ask for help: say who you need, what happened, and that it is important. Children practice in pairs with a card. Used when hurt, lost, or suddenly sick. Serves HECAT.S.HBO7.

When a worry or big feeling will not go away, ask a trusted adult for help and listen to what they say. Children rehearse "I feel ___ and I need help." This is the non-sensitive route to help in mental and emotional health, and the worry scene practices the help steps (~NHES.S3.2.2), so standard 3 is practiced outside safety; no child is asked about their own feelings or family. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO4.

What to say or do when something feels wrong or unsafe: say stop, move away, tell a trusted adult, keep telling until help comes. Scenes: a game gets rough, a stranger asks for something, a place feels scary. Practiced with scripts, with an adult playing any pressure. Carries the kindergarten rule: a found vape, lighter or pills: leave it, tell an adult. Serves HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO6, HECAT.V.HBO7.
Some choices need a grown-up's help. Children sort choices they make alone from those that need help (crossing a road, a medicine, a found item). Serves HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5.

Decision steps 2 and 3: name two or three options and what could happen with each, using snack choices. Options all stay foods that help or foods for sometimes; no scolding either way. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO1, HECAT.FN.HBO3.
A goal is a healthy thing I want to do ("I will wash before lunch"). Children say their goal in the frame and why it helps their body or mind. Safe list only. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2.
Who can help me reach my goal (a teacher, a family member, a friend) and two or three steps in order, drawn as pictures. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1.
Ways to help others make healthy and safe choices: remind a friend to buckle up, tell an adult when a friend is hurt, share a safe idea. Children name two ways. Serves HECAT.S.HBO8.

Small problems on the playground can be settled with words, taking turns or getting an adult. Children practice "Stop, I don't like that" and asking an adult when words do not work. Serves HECAT.V.HBO1, HECAT.V.HBO3, HECAT.V.HBO7.
The people who give medicine safely (parents, doctors, nurses, pharmacists) and why we ask before taking anything. Never test knowledge of home medicines. Serves HECAT.AOD.HBO1.

words: private; safe touch; unsafe touch; tell; no secret
notes: Sensitive unit (removable). Teacher note: leave-out note and family note as in grade K; the course still reaches asking for help in g1-s-ask-for-help. Body safety repeated with scenes about whom to tell and what to say when the first adult does not help: keep telling. No child is asked about their own experience; teach disclosure handling to adults (listen, no secrecy promise, school duty to report). Serves HECAT.V.HBO8.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in k-v-kind-words-and-hands and g1-phw-how-things-touch-me. Teacher note: families vary in structure, culture and faith; use warm neutral words and let the school or family decide. Many kinds of families and friendships, and respect for every person whatever they look like or who they are. No body or reproduction content here. Serves HECAT.SH.HBO2, HECAT.SH.HBO3.

Why being healthy and feeling well matters: energy to play and learn, feeling happy, being with friends. Children give a reason in a sentence and tie it to a habit they have done. Also reuses strengths from grade 1. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2.

words: germs; spread; vaccine; clean; stay home
notes: Practicing the germ habits at a deeper level: where germs hide (shared objects), why we stay home when sick, and that vaccines help protect people (a fact, no stories of illness). Practiced as habits for the class. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5.

When a visit to a doctor or nurse is a good idea (very hot, hurt that will not stop, a checkup) and that a trusted adult decides and goes with you. Children say who they tell. Care-seeking starts here (PHW 11 in the K to 2 map). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO11.

The same thing can touch two people differently (loud music, a food, a new place), so listen before judging. Children use the listening steps and the influence check on a short scene. Listening is carried from kindergarten through grade 1; both grades touch it. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO7.

Find the people who help with health at school and nearby: school nurse, teacher, counselor, crossing guard, firefighter, doctor. Children map two helpers and what each helps with. Families differ; the map starts at school. Serves HECAT.S.HBO7.

Personal limits in plain scenes: a friend's grab, a tickle that goes on, a borrowed toy, personal space. Steps: say it, say stop again, move away, tell. Children also honor others' limits when they say stop. Introduces boundary steps. Serves HECAT.V.HBO3, HECAT.V.HBO7.

Decision step 4: pick the option that is best for your body and give a reason ("It gives me energy to play"). Several answers fit; the reason matters, not the choice. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO1, HECAT.FN.HBO3.

Act on the goal for a week with a picture chart and a helper. Every child acts at school (a movement-break goal with the classroom teacher); a character's chart shows understanding only. Children tell what they did, not how well. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2.
Look back on the goal: what worked, what was hard, what next. A goal that did not work is information, not failure. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1.

Encourage others to be active: invite someone who is left out, cheer, share a game. Children practice an invite line. The class's movement-break goal (g2-phw-goal-do-it) applies the goal plan to physical activity (~NHES.S6.2.5). Shared with PE. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1.
"No thanks" and walk away if someone offers a cigarette or vape, then tell a trusted adult. Short scripted scene with a card playing the offer. Serves HECAT.T.HBO1, HECAT.T.HBO2.

Getting help when you or a friend is hurt or suddenly sick: stay safe, go get an adult, say what happened. First look at calling for emergency help: get an adult first; if no adult can help, call 911 (practiced on a paper phone). Taught non-sensitively. Serves HECAT.S.HBO7.

Safety rules for water, bikes, fire and kitchens, and noticing a dangerous place and staying away. Children state the reason behind each rule. Carries medicine safety: medicines and cleaners stay with adults. Serves HECAT.S.HBO1, HECAT.S.HBO3, HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5, HECAT.S.HBO6.
Choosing a calm tool and then telling someone how I feel with the I-statement. Children practice both in order: calm first, talk second. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO1, HECAT.MEH.HBO4, HECAT.MEH.HBO5.

Settle a small conflict with words: stop, say what happened, listen, find a fair way. Introduces conflict steps in short form. Fights are not a choice; an adult helps when words do not work. Serves HECAT.V.HBO1, HECAT.MEH.HBO3.

words: private; safe touch; unsafe touch; tell
notes: Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g2-v-my-limits-say-stop and g2-s-find-school-helpers. Teacher note: leave-out note and family note as in earlier years. Body safety with the helper map from g2-s-find-school-helpers: who to tell at home, at school and nearby. Reinforces that a child is never to blame. Serves HECAT.V.HBO8.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g2-v-my-limits-say-stop and k-phw-wellness-parts. Teacher note: the school or family decides; children whose bodies change early may be affected by leaving it out. Bodies grow and change in many ways; privacy and respect for others' limits; correct names are already taught in k-phw-body-names. Age-matched with no reproduction detail. Serves HECAT.SH.HBO1, HECAT.SH.HBO2.

Explain how to grow a strength that keeps me healthy (a calm routine, a sport skill, asking for help) by practicing it and finding a helper. Children write one way they could build a strength. Grade 1 strengths are reused (skips grade 2 as its own row; grade 2 revisits it inside g2-phw-why-health-matters). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

Name a healthy action for each part of wellness (physical, mental and emotional, social). Children build a wellness wheel with one real action per part and say why it helps. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

words: habit; sleep; eyes; ears; skin; sun
notes: Look closely at habits that help me and others: enough sleep, wearing sunscreen and shades, safe volume, washing. Children name who benefits from each (me, my class). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO3, HECAT.PHW.HBO4.

Describe how various things shape a person's health and well-being: family, friends, media, school, the place we live. Influence check: name the influence, say how it pushes (toward or away from a healthy habit). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO6.

words: grain; fruit; vegetable; dairy; protein; whole grain
notes: The food groups and what each does for a growing body, with a range of foods from each group (including fortified dairy swaps). Foods that help every day and foods for sometimes; no calorie talk, no good and bad. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO1, HECAT.FN.HBO2, HECAT.FN.HBO3, HECAT.FN.HBO4, HECAT.FN.HBO5.

words: added sugar; label; sugary drink; water
notes: Added sugar and where it hides, reading the sugar line on a drink label, and why water and milk are the everyday drinks. Children read a label and compare two drinks. No shame about foods at home. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO7, HECAT.FN.HBO8, HECAT.FN.HBO6.

An hour of activity a day and the three kinds that build a heart, muscles and flexibility; warm up, cool down and drink water. Notice when someone is left out and invite them. Health teaches the why and a plan; PE teaches the moving. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1, HECAT.PA.HBO2, HECAT.PA.HBO3, HECAT.PA.HBO4, HECAT.PA.HBO7.

Communicate clearly what I think and need so it helps health: the I-statement with a reason and a request ("I feel ___ when ___ because ___. Please ___."). Practiced in scripts about a friend, a group and a teacher. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO1, HECAT.MEH.HBO2.

Careful listening in several places (class, a game, home, on a call): look, wait, ask one question, say back what you heard. Children rate their listening on a card. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO7, HECAT.MEH.HBO8.

Choose which adult or health resource fits which situation (a scraped knee, a worry, a lost item, a question about food). The second help step: pick the right helper and the right words. Serves HECAT.S.HBO7.

words: resource; clinic; library; hotline; school nurse
notes: Find wellness resources at home, at school and in the community (nurse, clinic, library, a trusted website a teacher names). Children build a one-page "where to go" list with a family or school adult. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5.

Identify situations that call for careful thinking before choosing: a dare, a medicine, a stranger online, a risky play spot. Children sort easy choices from careful ones. Serves HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5.

Set one health goal in a sentence and explain how it helps health. Goals come from the safe list (sleep, water, handwashing, time outside, screen breaks, a kind act, asking for help). Never weight or food limits. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2.
Decide whether a goal is best done alone, with a helper or as a team. Children sort goals (walking to school with friends, a family sleep routine) and give a reason. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2.

Safety at home, in a car, near water, on a bike, and online in the simplest form (ask before you click, no private details). Children decide for a set of cases and give the reason. Injury prevention is about rules and choices, never blame. Serves HECAT.S.HBO1, HECAT.S.HBO3, HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5, HECAT.S.HBO6.

Medicines are used only as directed by a trusted adult. First plain facts about alcohol: it is not for children and why. Topic returns after grade 2 (skips grade 2 on purpose: grade 2 covers other topics). No child is asked about home. Serves HECAT.AOD.HBO1, HECAT.AOD.HBO2, HECAT.AOD.HBO3.

What nicotine is, what vapor and smoke do to lungs and to people near them, and why most people your age do not use them (stated as the approach page says for grades below 6, where no national use survey of this age exists). Influence check on an ad. No scare images. Serves HECAT.T.HBO1, HECAT.T.HBO2, HECAT.T.HBO3, HECAT.T.HBO4.

Bullying is repeated unkind acts that hurt; roles are the one bullied, the one bullying, and bystanders who can help. Children practice an upstander line and telling an adult. No role-play of bullying; a card plays the unkind line. Serves HECAT.V.HBO1, HECAT.V.HBO3.

Stating a limit (space, belongings, tickling, shared photos) and respecting others' limits. Boundary steps: say it, repeat it, leave, tell. Non-sensitive; the sensitive unit practices the same steps. Serves HECAT.V.HBO3, HECAT.V.HBO1.

words: privacy; unsafe touch; tell; trusted adult
notes: Sensitive unit (removable). Teacher note: leave-out note and family note; the course still reaches help in g3-s-which-helper and limits in g3-v-my-limits-and-yours. Body safety with practice telling more than one adult and the idea that abuse is never a child's fault. Teachers hear disclosures with the school's duty to report; never promise secrecy. Serves HECAT.V.HBO8, HECAT.V.HBO9.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g3-meh-listening and g4-v-limits-and-respect. Teacher note: the school or family decides. Respect for every person whatever their family, gender or who they like, and what makes a healthy friendship. No puberty content here. Serves HECAT.SH.HBO2, HECAT.SH.HBO3.

Explain ways to make illness and injury less likely: vaccines, handwashing, food and water safety, rest, gear. Children sort a set of illnesses and injuries by which habit helps. States the one fact needed (germs spread by touch, air, food and water; vaccines teach the body to defend itself) and gives its source. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5, HECAT.PHW.HBO8.

Show healthy routines, including how people care for a long-term condition such as asthma, an allergy or diabetes. Teacher note: do not ask about conditions in the room; a condition is never a blame or a weakness. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO9.

Work out how these things affect my health and others' health, with a real case: screen time and sleep, a friend's choice and mine. Children pick one influence to counter with a habit. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO6.
One factor can affect people and communities in different ways (a hot day with or without shade, a snack ad, a park nearby). The reason is circumstance, not a person's worth. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO7.

cross_subject: ela:RI.4.8 (explain how an author uses reasons and evidence for a claim)
notes: Judge whether a health fact, product or service (a snack ad, a label, a drink claim, a flyer for a health service) is correct and can be trusted. Introduces the source check: who made it, what they want, is there evidence, does an adult I trust agree. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO8.

Show how to ask for help and give it, including help with a sad or worried feeling: pick an adult, use the I-statement, ask for one thing, and thank them; also how to be the one who listens when a friend asks. The help-seeking outcome for mental and emotional health in this band is taught here in a non-sensitive unit. Teacher note: help line named in plain words. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO4, HECAT.MEH.HBO5.

Get help in an emergency: what counts as one, how an adult calls for help, how a child can give a name and place. Practiced without real calls. Taught a second time in a non-sensitive unit so help never depends on a sensitive unit. Serves HECAT.S.HBO7.

Set personal limits and respect the limits of others in friendships and games and online: ask, listen for a yes or no, accept it. Consent for non-body activities (sharing a photo, borrowing, joining a game). Serves HECAT.V.HBO3, HECAT.MEH.HBO8.

Refusal steps: say no clearly, give a short reason or none, suggest another thing, leave. Scripted rehearsal on offers of a vape, a dare and a snack. A card plays the offer; no student plays a pressurer. Serves HECAT.T.HBO1, HECAT.T.HBO4.
Decide whether a health decision needs someone's help or a team (a medicine, an online question, a friend in trouble). Children sort decisions by who should help. Serves HECAT.S.HBO5.

Compare options and what each is likely to lead to using an everyday food choice and a safety choice. Children fill a two-column chart of "if I do this, then ...". Serves HECAT.FN.HBO8, HECAT.FN.HBO10.

A goal plan with actions, resources and a way to check progress. Children write a one-week plan for a safe-list goal. The first plan can build a strength (from grade 3). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2.
Identify what helps and what blocks progress toward a goal (time, a friend, a space) and one way around a block. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2.

Notice when speaking up could help my own or another person's health or safety: someone being left out, a friend ignoring a helmet rule. Children name who they would tell and what they would say. Serves HECAT.V.HBO3, HECAT.V.HBO7.

How teamwork and clear communication make speaking up stronger: a small team asks for more handwashing time or a shade structure with one clear message. Introduces the speak-up plan (notice, who, say, ask). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5, HECAT.PA.HBO7.

words: warm up; cool down; fitness; flexibility
notes: Warm up, cool down, drink water and stop when hurt; plan an activity week that supports growth. Shared with PE. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO2, HECAT.PA.HBO3, HECAT.PA.HBO5, HECAT.PA.HBO6.

Heading off and coping with stress and worry: notice the signs, pick a tool (breath, a walk, talking), tell. Children rate their tools; no child is asked about their worries. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO4, HECAT.MEH.HBO5.

Sensitive unit (removable). Teacher note: leave-out note and family note. Unwanted touch and abuse in plain words: never a child's fault, telling works, tell until someone helps. Practice with a written tell-script and a list of helpers. The course still teaches limits in g4-v-limits-and-respect and asking for help in g4-meh-help-with-feelings and g4-s-get-help-emergency. If a student tells you: listen, no secrecy promise, follow the duty to report, name the next adult. Serves HECAT.V.HBO8, HECAT.V.HBO9.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g4-v-limits-and-respect and g4-meh-help-with-feelings. Teacher note: school or family decides; children whose bodies change early are affected by leaving this out, so the school offers a private route. Puberty in plain correct terms before it starts: body changes, hygiene, that timing varies and all are normal, and who to ask. Serves HECAT.SH.HBO1.

Examine how knowing how to find and use health information helps wellness: search with an adult, read a label, ask a nurse, check with the source check. Children write how info would change a choice. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5, HECAT.PHW.HBO6.

words: environment; community; clean air; water; safe
notes: How surroundings shape the health of a person and a community: air, water, parks, housing, food access. Children map one community feature and its effect. No blame for a neighborhood. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO6.

When to get health care and the reasons: checkups, vaccines, a long-lasting cough, an injury; who takes you and who to tell. Teacher note: access to care differs; point to school nurse and community clinics. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO10, HECAT.PHW.HBO11.

words: screen time; ad; peer pressure; tool
notes: Use tools and resources to deal with things that affect wellness: screen limits and an adult, muting an account, a friend to back me up. Children pick a tool for each influence. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO2, HECAT.MEH.HBO9.

Describe how wrong or misleading health claims can hurt people (a miracle drink, a sugary snack sold as healthy, a ruined routine). Practice the source check on three claims. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO8, HECAT.PHW.HBO12.

Stay out of, handle and settle conflicts: stop, calm down, each person says their side, find a fair way, or walk away and get help. Written scripts for three conflicts. Conflict steps carried from grade 2. Serves HECAT.V.HBO1, HECAT.V.HBO2, HECAT.MEH.HBO3.

Speak and act with care and kindness, including when we disagree: a kind word to a friend, including a new student, an apology. Also reuses grade 3 listening (carried). Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO7, HECAT.MEH.HBO8.

Facts about alcohol and other drugs that matter for a decision, what most students really do (stated as the approach page says for grades below 6, where no national use survey of this age exists), and refusal steps from grade 4 on a new scenario. Medicine misuse is included. Serves HECAT.AOD.HBO1, HECAT.AOD.HBO2, HECAT.AOD.HBO3.

Choose the option that supports health or safety using the full decision steps, on a new scenario. Includes the injury-prevention link back to ~NHES.S1.5.3. Serves HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5, HECAT.S.HBO6.
Think about how a decision turned out for them and others, for a character: what I would keep and change. Students are not asked to reveal their own decisions. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO5.
Keep track of progress toward a health goal with a chart or log and one check-in with a helper. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2.
Reflect on how setting the goal went and what resulted. A missed goal is a reason to change the plan, not a verdict on the student. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2.
Practice healthy habits for several weeks (activity, water, rest) with a log and a partner. Shared with PE; the plan is health's. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1, HECAT.PA.HBO2, HECAT.PA.HBO3, HECAT.PA.HBO5.

Name advocacy skills and approaches (a poster, a letter, a team ask, a talk) for tobacco-free places and helping friends stay free of tobacco. The class picks an approach and who the audience is. Serves HECAT.T.HBO3, HECAT.T.HBO4.

Show how to speak up for safety and wellness: a short talk to a younger class, a note to the principal about a safety problem. Practiced and delivered to a real audience. Serves HECAT.S.HBO8, HECAT.V.HBO7.

Digital safety inside safety: keep private details private, refuse a request from a stranger, tell an adult about a message that feels wrong. No lessons on any app by name. Serves HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5, HECAT.V.HBO5.

Habits that support mental and emotional health (time outside, a friend, a creative thing, sleep) and the strengths that help me cope. Reuses grade 3 strengths (skips grade 4 as its own row; grade 4 meh unit covers stress). Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO2, HECAT.MEH.HBO9.

Help others eat in healthy ways: plan a class snack day with fruit and vegetable choices and a way to include every food culture. Teacher note: families' foods and budgets differ and are never ranked. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO12.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. A steady yearly repeat at a slightly deeper level: signs that a touch or a secret is not okay, adults at school and a hotline named in plain words, and that a child is never to blame. The course still meets these skills in g4-v-limits-and-respect and g5-v-conflict-steps, and carries help in g5-phw-when-to-get-care and g5-s-online-safety. Serves HECAT.V.HBO8, HECAT.V.HBO9.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g4-v-limits-and-respect and g5-phw-when-to-get-care. Teacher note: school or family decides; children whose bodies change early are affected by leaving this out, so the school offers a private route. Puberty review, consent as an everyday rule (ask, listen for yes, a no is final), and basic facts that HIV and other infections are medical conditions people live with and can be prevented. Correct terms, no reproduction detail beyond the tool's span expectations. Serves HECAT.SH.HBO1, HECAT.SH.HBO4, HECAT.SH.HBO6.

Analyze how strengths raise wellness for one person or a whole group: a strength shared on a team, a class, a family. Students map strengths of a character group and what each adds. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

Analyze how habits support each part of wellness and how parts affect each other (sleep and mood, activity and focus). Students build a cause-and-effect chain. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

Analyze behaviors that keep illness and injury from happening or lessen them, stating the one fact needed (germs spread by touch, air, food and water; vaccines teach the body to defend itself) with its source: vaccines, handwashing, food safety, helmets, sun protection, hearing protection. Students compare how much each behavior lowers risk. Returns to g4-phw-prevent-illness-injury after a skip: grade 5 carries only the injury side (g5-s-choose-safe-option), and illness prevention has no grade 5 row, on purpose. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5, HECAT.PHW.HBO6, HECAT.PHW.HBO8, HECAT.PHW.HBO3, HECAT.PHW.HBO4.

Study how different influences link and act on each other (media shapes what peers do; family shapes what media I see). Influence check with two linked influences on a character. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO6, HECAT.MEH.HBO9.

Identify situations where a trusted adult or a health professional is needed: persistent pain, an injury, long-lasting sadness, a symptom that worries you. Students choose the right helper and the first sentence to say. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO10, HECAT.PHW.HBO11.

What makes it easier or harder to reach reliable information and help: cost, distance, language, privacy, fear of being judged. Students name one barrier and one way around it. Serves HECAT.S.HBO7, HECAT.PHW.HBO10.

words: message; tone; text; face to face
notes: Communicate well in several ways (speaking, writing, a message, an email) for my own good and others', and notice that the same words land differently by channel. Students rewrite a message so it supports health. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO1, HECAT.MEH.HBO8.
Careful listening in many face-to-face situations, including when the topic is hard or the person is upset. Students use the listening steps with a partner on a scripted scene. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO8.

Explain how following the decision steps affects health, using an eating-out choice. Students compare a quick choice and a step-by-step one. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO1, HECAT.FN.HBO2, HECAT.FN.HBO3, HECAT.FN.HBO9.

Decide when a health situation calls for a careful decision process: an offer, a dare, a friend's invitation. Students sort a set into "easy", "careful" and "get help now". Serves HECAT.T.HBO1, HECAT.T.HBO2.

Assess my own health to pick areas to set goals in using a habit self-check (sleep, water, activity, screen breaks, friends). Never measures of weight or shape; the self-check stays with the student. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.
Decide when to set goals alone, with help or in a group. Students pick the best form for several goals and give the reason. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2.

cross_subject: math:6.SP.B.5 (summarize a data set for a behavior log, after the grade 6 statistics unit)
notes: Study what supports healthy habits and what stands in the way (time, access, friends, weather, cost) using a class or character activity log. Shared with PE. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1, HECAT.PA.HBO2, HECAT.PA.HBO5.

Nicotine and tobacco facts for a decision and the influences behind use (marketing, peers, family). A current national survey figure for the age group, with source and year, shows most students do not use them. Help to quit is named. Serves HECAT.T.HBO1, HECAT.T.HBO2, HECAT.T.HBO3, HECAT.T.HBO4, HECAT.T.HBO5.

Facts a decision needs about alcohol, other drugs and misuse of medicine at this age, with real use figures (source and year). No scare images; teacher note on the range of experiences in a room. Serves HECAT.AOD.HBO1, HECAT.AOD.HBO2, HECAT.AOD.HBO3, HECAT.AOD.HBO4.

Bullying and harassment in person and online, boundaries to say stop, and how to report. Students write a response script and a report. Never role-play the person who bullies. Serves HECAT.V.HBO1, HECAT.V.HBO3, HECAT.V.HBO7.

cross_subject: math:6.RP.A.3 (ratio and percent reasoning on a label, after the grade 6 ratio unit)
notes: A healthy eating pattern that fits needs, tastes, culture and budget; reading a label and a serving with ratio reasoning from math. No weighing, no calorie counting, no good or bad foods; foods that help and foods to have less often. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO1, HECAT.FN.HBO2, HECAT.FN.HBO3, HECAT.FN.HBO4, HECAT.FN.HBO5, HECAT.FN.HBO6, HECAT.FN.HBO7, HECAT.FN.HBO8, HECAT.FN.HBO9.

Heading off and coping with stress and worry in healthy ways; notice signs; choose habits and tell a trusted adult. Includes where to find help in plain words. Non-sensitive. Returns to g4-meh-calm-stress after a skip: the idea is not taught in between, on purpose. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO2, HECAT.MEH.HBO4, HECAT.MEH.HBO5, HECAT.MEH.HBO9.
Notice chances to speak up for the safety and health of others at school (a hazard, a rule, a person left out) and plan what to say. Serves HECAT.S.HBO8.

Sensitive unit (removable). Teacher note: leave-out note and family note; help is also taught in g6-phw-adult-or-professional and g6-s-reach-reliable-help. Unwanted or wrong touching and sexual harassment in plain, factual terms, how to tell a trusted adult or a help line, and that blame is never the victim's. Follow the school's duty to report; for a parent teaching at home, the national child abuse hotline and the 988 crisis line are named by purpose and a disclosure is not handled alone. Serves HECAT.V.HBO8, HECAT.V.HBO9.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g6-phw-habits-for-each-part and g6-meh-communicate-ways. Teacher note: leave-out note names who is affected (students whose bodies change early) and the school or family decides. Puberty with correct terms for bodies of all kinds, hygiene, respect for every identity, healthy and unhealthy relationship signs. Serves HECAT.SH.HBO1, HECAT.SH.HBO2, HECAT.SH.HBO3.

Analyze healthy routines, including living with a health condition, and the supports people need (medicines, a plan at school). Characters live full lives; no blame. Characters name strengths and supports that help them. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO9.
Analyze how skill with health information links to how healthy people are: understanding a label, a dosage direction, a vaccine record. Students decode a sample instruction. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO10.

Examine personal, group, community, society and environment factors (culture, price, nearby stores, ads, what grows or is sold nearby) behind eating choices, their health results and fairness in health, without ranking any food culture. Influence check at all five levels. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO11.
Analyze why influences land differently on groups and communities (parks, safe routes, time, cost). Students compare two community profiles. Never blame a group. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1, HECAT.PA.HBO2.

cross_subject: ela:RI.7.8 (evaluate claims and the evidence given)
notes: Get health information, products and services from credible sources: government health agency, a hospital, a national medical body. Students trace a claim to its source, and name a credible place to get a health product (a pharmacy) and a service (a school nurse, a clinic). Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO10.

cross_subject: ela:RI.7.8 (evaluate claims and the evidence given)
notes: Assess whether a health resource is correct, trustworthy and within reach, using food and supplement claims and a wellness fad. Students rate each on three questions. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO8, HECAT.FN.HBO9, HECAT.PHW.HBO12.

Use methods to seek support and give it: tell a trusted adult, check on a friend, share a help line. Includes a friend who seems very down: stay, listen, tell an adult at once. Non-sensitive entry to help; the self-harm unit extends it. Stops at 'tell an adult'; self-harm is g7-meh-self-harm-help. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO4, HECAT.MEH.HBO8.

State boundaries and say whether I agree to an activity: group chats, shared photos, a ride, a game. Say yes, say no, change my mind. Boundary steps in digital and in-person settings. Serves HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5, HECAT.V.HBO5.

Use ways to turn down requests (alcohol, a vape, riding with an impaired driver) in many settings: a direct no, an excuse, a switch, a text for a ride. Scripts only; a card plays the pressure. Serves HECAT.AOD.HBO3, HECAT.AOD.HBO4, HECAT.AOD.HBO6.

Apply methods to prevent, handle and end conflicts: calm, listen, I-statements, a neutral helper, a clean apology. Fights are not an option; when a person is not safe, walk away and tell. Serves HECAT.V.HBO1, HECAT.V.HBO2, HECAT.V.HBO6.
Use a decision process alone, with help or in a group: for a risky ride, a group dare, an online request. Students choose the form that fits and say why. Serves HECAT.S.HBO4, HECAT.S.HBO5.
Judge how each option could affect health at personal and wider levels: skipping a team practice, a school fundraiser, a family routine. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1, HECAT.PA.HBO5.
Write a goal and explain its link to health with a measure and a time. Safe list or a self-chosen healthy behavior; never weight, calories or shape. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.
Build a plan that deals with supports and barriers: a backup for the missed day, a helper, a change of place. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.
Break down which habits improve personal and community wellness (sleep, screens, handwashing, helping a neighbor) and compare their reach. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

Examine chances to speak up for the health of individuals, families and communities: a crosswalk, a school lunch, a heat plan. Students choose one real chance and write a one-line ask. Serves HECAT.S.HBO8.

cross_subject: ela:W.7.1 (write an argument with claims and evidence)
notes: Decide whether to advocate alone or in a group for a given situation (a tobacco-free school, a vape-free event) and plan the first step. Serves HECAT.T.HBO3, HECAT.T.HBO4.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. Teacher note: no method detail, no lesson without a help line and an adult plan; safe-messaging rules; a counselor knows a lesson is coming and is on call. Students learn signs a friend needs help, what to say and who to tell at once, and that it is never a secret to keep. The course still teaches support and help in g6-phw-adult-or-professional and g7-meh-seek-and-give-support (non-sensitive units). Students are not asked about their own feelings. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO6, HECAT.V.HBO10.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g7-s-online-boundaries and g7-meh-seek-and-give-support. Teacher note: leave-out note and family note. Healthy and unhealthy relationship signs, sexual harassment, consent as a clear freely given yes, and where to get help. Respect for every person; never blame. Students rehearse written refusal lines; cards play any pressure. Serves HECAT.V.HBO4, HECAT.V.HBO8, HECAT.V.HBO9.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g7-s-online-boundaries and g7-meh-seek-and-give-support. Teacher note: school or family decides; inclusive of every identity. Healthy relationships, consent, choosing not to have sex, never pressuring anyone, and respect for gender identity and sexual orientation. No scare tactics, no shame. Serves HECAT.SH.HBO2, HECAT.SH.HBO3, HECAT.SH.HBO4, HECAT.SH.HBO5, HECAT.SH.HBO9.

words: passenger; seat belt; driver; helmet; gear; alone; dangerous place
notes: Safety as students start riding with older drivers and going out alone (Cory, 2026-11-20): buckle up and ride in the back seat, never ride with a driver who has used alcohol or drugs or is driving unsafely, and plan another way home; wear the right gear for bikes, boards and scooters and wear it right; notice dangerous places (water, tracks, building sites, empty lots) and stay away. Students rehearse turning down a ride and calling for another one from written scripts; a card plays the driver, and no student plays an impaired driver. Serves HECAT.S.HBO1, HECAT.S.HBO2, HECAT.S.HBO3, HECAT.S.HBO6.

Analyze how personal, social, community and environmental factors each affect health, with a case such as asthma and air quality or sleep and school start time. Returns to g5-phw-surroundings-community after a skip: the idea is not taught in between, on purpose. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO6.

Explain how health care services help keep a person healthy: checkups, vaccines, dental, vision, school nurse, urgent care and what each is for. Teacher note: access and cost differ. Returns to g6-phw-adult-or-professional after a skip: the idea is not taught in between, on purpose. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO10, HECAT.PHW.HBO11.

Put methods and tools into practice to deal with what affects wellness: social media limits, ad analysis, a pause rule, talking with a friend. Students test a tool for a week with a log they keep private. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO2, HECAT.MEH.HBO9.

cross_subject: ela:RI.8.8 (evaluate an argument and its evidence)
notes: Use strategies for handling false and misleading health messages: stop, check the source, find a second source, tell what is false kindly. Students fact-check three posts. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO10.
Work well with others in different settings: roles, giving credit, handling a person who does not help. Students plan a team health project. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO8.
Use negotiation and compromise: say what each side needs, offer trades, agree on a fair plan; a limit is not up for negotiation. Serves HECAT.V.HBO1, HECAT.MEH.HBO3.

Talk with people whose views or values differ: ask to understand, find common ground, disagree kindly. Students rehearse on a food example, a screen-time example and one example about a belief or custom, worded to stay neutral on faith. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO7, HECAT.MEH.HBO8.
Show understanding and concern for others: noticing, a check-in line, offering help, knowing when to tell an adult. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO8, HECAT.MEH.HBO7.
Name the supports and obstacles shaping a decision at different levels (friends, family, school, laws, ads) for a decision about alcohol or other drugs. Serves HECAT.AOD.HBO3, HECAT.AOD.HBO4.
Assess how a health decision worked out for me and others, for a character and for a school activity, and what to change. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO1, HECAT.PA.HBO5.
Monitor progress and decide whether to keep or change the goal or plan, with a simple log or chart. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.
Examine how setting the goal affected health and well-being, including what to carry into the next goal. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.
Carry out habits that support personal and community wellness (a service of handwashing posters, a walking group, a sleep routine) for several weeks. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

cross_subject: ela:W.8.1 (write an argument for an audience)
notes: Fit advocacy approaches to the audience and setting: a school lunch ask to a principal, a note to a family, a post for peers. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO12.
Practice advocacy methods that improve wellness for me and others: a short talk, a flyer, an invitation to join. Delivered to a real audience. Serves HECAT.PA.HBO7.
Judge whether advocacy really made health better: what changed, how we know, what to try next. Serves HECAT.S.HBO8.
Tobacco influences at wider levels (advertising, flavors, price, laws) and tools to counter them; quitting is hard and help exists. Serves HECAT.T.HBO1, HECAT.T.HBO3, HECAT.T.HBO5.

Planning how to avoid riding with a driver who has used alcohol or other drugs: a family plan, a call or text, a safe ride code. Facts only; no scare images. Serves HECAT.AOD.HBO3, HECAT.AOD.HBO4, HECAT.AOD.HBO6, HECAT.S.HBO2, HECAT.AOD.HBO8.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g8-v-negotiate-compromise and g8-meh-different-views. Teacher note: leave-out note and family note. Healthy and unhealthy relationship signs, coercion, sexual assault named factually, consent, and where to get help. Never blame; rehearsal is written refusal lines only; a disclosure is never handled alone. Serves HECAT.V.HBO4, HECAT.V.HBO8, HECAT.V.HBO9.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g8-meh-express-concern and g8-meh-teamwork. Teacher note: no method detail, a help line and an adult plan are on the first page, safe-messaging rules, counselor on call. Warning signs, what to say to a friend, who to tell right away, and where help is. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO6, HECAT.V.HBO10.

Sensitive unit (removable). Leave-out note and family note before it as STANDARD.md section 5 says; the disclosure steps are on the approach page. The course still meets these skills in g8-v-negotiate-compromise and g8-meh-different-views. Teacher note: school or family decides; medically accurate, inclusive, no shame. How pregnancy happens and ways to prevent it, how infections spread and are prevented, testing and where health services are, and how to help a friend get accurate information. Serves HECAT.SH.HBO5, HECAT.SH.HBO6, HECAT.SH.HBO7, HECAT.SH.HBO8, HECAT.SH.HBO10.

Apply ways to build strengths that help individual and shared health, and analyze how the parts of wellness connect to results. Revisits grade 6 strengths at a deeper level in one row. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO1, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

Evaluate behaviors for how well they prevent or reduce illness and injury, and habits for supporting health, including care for ongoing conditions. Uses grade 6 and 7 analysis and does not rebuild it. Returns to g7-phw-living-with-conditions after a skip: the idea is not taught in between, on purpose. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO5, HECAT.PHW.HBO6, HECAT.PHW.HBO9.

Analyze how factors at many levels connect and shape results, what helps or blocks a behavior, and how confidence in my ability and my sense of risk change behavior. Students use a short case on sleep or physical activity. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO6, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

How easy it is to reach trusted adults, professionals and services, what opens or blocks access to trustworthy information and care, and how that relates to wellness. Students map options in a community, including confidential care. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO10, HECAT.PHW.HBO11.

cross_subject: ela:RI.8.8 (evaluate an argument and its evidence)
notes: Examine how health information skill of people and organizations shapes outcomes; rate resources on accuracy, trustworthiness and availability; choose and use accurate sources on a food or supplement question. Serves HECAT.FN.HBO1, HECAT.FN.HBO8, HECAT.PHW.HBO12.

Use approaches that push back on misinformation and deliberate disinformation about mental health, drugs, diets or wellness trends: pause, trace, counter kindly, report. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO2, HECAT.MEH.HBO9.

Judge how influences and behaviors act on each other and on well-being, design a plan to handle the influences on my health, and use available resources. The plan is personal and not shared unless the student chooses. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO2, HECAT.MEH.HBO4, HECAT.MEH.HBO9.

Assess how social conditions such as income and neighborhood shape behaviors and results, and how factors from the personal to the environmental affect fairness in health. Teacher note: families and neighborhoods in the room vary; study places, not people. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO6.
Communicate effectively through many channels (talk, text, social media, email) and across different relationships (a friend, an employer, a doctor). Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO1, HECAT.MEH.HBO8.

Ask for and give help for health, and express understanding and concern for others in a range of situations, including a friend who is struggling. Taught in a non-sensitive unit; the self-harm unit extends it. Serves HECAT.MEH.HBO4, HECAT.MEH.HBO8.

Use skills to state limits, give or take back consent and set boundaries in varied situations (friendships, work, online, shared spaces). Non-sensitive; the sensitive units practice the same steps. Carry out a plan that deals with supports and barriers, monitor and revise it, and evaluate what the goal did for health. Serves HECAT.PHW.HBO2, HECAT.PHW.HBO7.

Judge how habits and other factors support wellness for people and groups, and show a range of habits that support wellness (cooking and sharing meals on a budget).
